messages:
Anya (CS): Heads-up — Shoreline reported a sudden p99 jump on /v1/embeddings starting ~17:10 UTC. Customer impact: slow searches in prod, some timeouts. They pasted a few request IDs: req_8a3f, req_8b2c, req_8d5e.

Sam (oncall): Acknowledged. Any correlation with deploys or config changes? Can you paste example curl and a sample request id with full headers?

Anya (CS): No deploys on their tenant. Example they sent: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n -H \"Authorization: Bearer tk_shoreline\" \n -d '{"input": "How do I reset my device?"}'```

Eli (infra): I'm pulling traces. Running a quick query on per-tenant tail latency in the last 30m.

Eli (infra): ```sql\nSELECT tenant, p95, p99, qps FROM inference_metrics WHERE tenant='shoreline' AND ts > now() - interval '30 minutes';\n-- result: shoreline p95=210ms p99=2.3s qps=48\n-- cluster avg p99 = 180ms\n```

Eli (infra): Looks like p99 elevated to ~2s for embeddings only. Checking active workers...

infra-bot: Detected high conn count for tenant=shoreline on node-gpu-12: conns=312, avg-kv-latency=1.9s. Alert created: ALERT-7382.

Sam (oncall): That conn count is suspicious. Could be noisy neighbor inside their tenant (heavy parallel batches) or an external bot loop. Julian, can you check if they recently switched to bulk requests or have a change in client SDK?

Julian (support): Reached out to Shoreline for repro. They confirmed a nightly job started rolling yesterday sending concurrent embed bulk calls (~200 concurrent). They thought it was limited to 5 workers but misconfigured to 200.

Anya (CS): Customer accepts it's their job but they need immediate relief while they fix it. Requested a short-term fix that doesn't require them to change code right now.

Eli (infra): Two options: 1) apply a per-tenant concurrency cap (throttle) to smooth tail 2) add them to a reservation/priority queue (if we want to keep latency stable but consume capacity). I'd push for a temporary concurrency throttle so other tenants unaffected.

Sam (oncall): Agreed. Please apply a soft throttle: cap concurrency to 40 and enforce circuit fallback at 3s. Use the control-plane CLI.

Eli (infra): Running command now: ```rictl tenant throttle set --tenant=shoreline --concurrency=40 --p99-fallback=3000ms --reason='temp-mitigation-2187654321'```

deploy-bot: Throttle policy applied for tenant=shoreline by eli; policy-id=tp-9921; propagation to edge nodes in progress.

infra-bot: Node-gpu-12 conn for shoreline reduced from 312 -> 34 within 90s after policy enforcement.

Sam (oncall): Can we confirm p99 dropped? Eli, can you post the same query after 5 min?

Eli (infra): Re-run query: ```-- 5m after policy: shoreline p95=190ms p99=260ms qps=37```

Anya (CS): Customer confirmed UX improved and timeouts stopped. They're going to fix the misconfigured job and asked if we can recommend long-term guardrails.

Julian (support): Suggested fixes to customer: add client-side rate limiter, exponential backoff, and use our batched-queue endpoint for bulk uploads. Also offered a short reservation if they need sustained burst.

Sam (oncall): Action items: 1) leave throttle in place for 2h, then re-evaluate (eli) 2) CS to follow up and confirm job fixed (anya) 3) infra to propose long-term auto-throttle/heuristics for sudden concurrency spikes (sam + eli).

Anya (CS): Shoreline asked about bypassing throttle for a specific partner account during their migration — they asked for an allowlist. We'll only do that if they sign a short-term reserved capacity agreement. Noted.

infra-bot: Reminder: create ticket INF-4159 to track auto-throttle feature.

Eli (infra): Throttle scheduled to auto-remove at 2187655521 unless extended. I'll monitor.

Sam (oncall): Nice quick win. Marking as mitigated for now. :white_check_mark:
